targets.title: Inaction inertia: Foregoing future benefits as a result of an initial failure to act.
targets.evidence_quote: We conducted three pre-registered replications of Tykocinski, Pittman, and Tuttle (1995) Experiments 1 and 2's four scenarios in four samples (N = 1555).
targets.outcome_quote: We conducted three pre-registered replications of the inaction inertia effect experiments by Tykocinski et al. (1995). Consistent with the findings in the target article, participants in the large-difference condition were less likely to act on the subsequent opportunity than participants in the small-difference condition. However, evidence regarding differences between the large- difference condition and the control condition was mixed. Furthermore, whereas the target article found no difference between the small-difference condition and the control condition, in our replication experiments, participants in the small-difference condition were more likely to act on the subsequent opportunity than participants in the control condition.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly distinguish supported comparisons from mixed and contrary comparisons, and report successful ski/car scenarios alongside a likely failed flyer scenario. Aggregate over the single original paper.

reasoning: Three preregistered experiments across four new samples retest Experiments 1 and 2 of one original paper. The primary author-hosted accepted manuscript includes the paper and its references before appended supplementary material. Other cited applications of inaction inertia and replication projects are background, not targets.
